item.title: The U.S. Army and a Second Manhattan Project for AI
item.description: To win the AI race, the U.S. Army must again serve as a national integrator—mobilizing talent, securing infrastructure, and modernizing forces, just as it did during the original Manhattan Project.

item.title: Lauryn Williams in The Washington Post: The cyberattacks are coming. Will anyone be there to stop them?
item.description: “Trump administration job cuts worsen U.S. vulnerabilities to China and other cyber-adversaries,” Williams warns.

item.title: Golden Dome for America: Assessing Chinese and Russian Reactions
item.description: This article surveys Chinese and Russian reactions to Golden Dome and develops an initial assessment of its potential impact on arms racing and strategic stability.

item.title: It’s Time for AI Policy to Get Serious About the AI Adoption Gap
item.description: In this latest piece, Shiva Goel and Matt Pearl argue that U.S. policy needs to double-down on AI adoption and propose a solution: rewarding colleges and universities that launch AI Adoption Accelerators to promote deployment in their local communities.

item.title: Keynote and Fireside Chat with General B. Chance Saltzman, Chief of Space Operations
item.description: General B. Chance Saltzman, Chief of Space Operations, joined the CSIS Aerospace Security Project for the Delivering Space Capabilities for Warfighting Advantage conference.

item.title: President Trump’s Redesignation of Nigeria as a “Country of Particular Concern—CPC”: A Serious, Well-founded Wake-up Call
item.description: The U.S.-Nigeria relationship is currently under friction. Whether and how Nigeria tackles its own governance and security challenges at home will set the pace not only in Nigeria, but also in the broader West Africa region.

item.title: U.S.-India Insight: Bihar’s Big Chance: Be Bold and Basic
item.description: The election may be over, but Bihar’s real challenge begins—finally shifting from laggard to leader in India’s growth story.

item.title: Force Design for the Twenty-First Century Fight: U.S. Cyber Force Lessons from China’s Strategic Support Forces
item.description: As the United States debates the creation of a standalone Cyber Force, it should learn the lessons China’s decade-long Strategic Support Force experiment offers in integrating space, cyber, and information capabilities for a new era of warfare.

item.title: What’s in the New U.S.-Saudi Minerals Agreement?
item.description: The U.S.-Saudi minerals partnership marks a realignment in global supply chains—pairing Saudi Arabia’s vast heavy rare earth reserves with significant U.S. investment to build a mine-to-magnet pathway that directly reduces China’s leverage and strengthens allied security.
